## What page 651 shows

Page 651 is **Helminthology, Plate CCLI (plate 251)**. The scan shows the running head "HELMINTHOLOGY." at top-left and "Plate CCLI." at top-right, with nine engraved figures labeled Fig. 1 through Fig. 9. These are parasitic worms (helminths):

- **Fig. 1** — a long, flat, ribbon-like worm (tapeworm/cestode)
- **Fig. 2** — an elongated segmented worm showing proglottids (tapeworm strobila)
- **Fig. 3** — a worm whose head (scolex) is armed with suckers and hooks
- **Fig. 4** — a coiled roundworm (nematode)
- **Fig. 5 & Fig. 6** — two oval objects with internal markings (worm eggs)
- **Fig. 7** — another segmented ribbon worm (tapeworm)
- **Fig. 8** — a small organism with a radiating, hook-armed proboscis (a thorny-headed/acanthocephalan-type worm), next to a segmented piece
- **Fig. 9** — a thick-bodied worm with a bulbous/clubbed posterior end

So the plate illustrates the helminths covered by the HELMINTHOLOGY article — tapeworms, roundworms, their eggs, scoleces, and a proboscis-armed worm. [B:651:0] (row 651) is the plate entry itself; its OCR reads "Fig 1 Fig.2. Fig.2. Fig.1. O Fig.3. Fig.3. Fig.8. Fig.7. Fig.9. Fig.9."

Bollnäs

Nordanstig

Ovanåker

Söderhamn

The coat of arms were granted in 1560 in the era of King Gustav Vasa. At that time, Hälsingland was known for its large scale goat breeding, and the arms depicted a standing goat facing heraldic right (blazon: Sable, a Goat rampant Or attired and hoofed Gules).

The terrain is mostly hilly and rocky, sloping down towards the coast. The highest elevation in the northern part is 530 meters, and 671 meters in the western part. Approximately 85% of the land area is covered with forest, and the timber industry has historically been the main source of income.

The earliest mention of the people of Hälsingland may be in the Old English poem Widsith, from the 9th or 10th century, where a people called the Hælsings are referred to. The first definite mention of the people is made by Adam of Bremen around 1070, in reference to the leidang shipping fleet.

results.title: Thorax
results.passage: Symptoms of this condition are often felt only on one side of the lung or as a shortness of breath. In mammals, the thorax is the region of the body formed by the sternum, the thoracic vertebrae, and the ribs. It extends from the neck to the diaphragm, and does not include the upper limbs. The heart and the lungs reside in the thoracic cavity, as well as many blood vessels. The inner organs are protected by the rib cage and the sternum. Thoracic vertebrae are also distinguished in birds, but not in reptiles. In insects, crustaceans, and the extinct trilobites, the thorax is the middle one of the three main divisions of the creature's body, each of which is in turn composed of multiple segments. It is the area where the wings and legs attach in insects, or an area of multiple articulating plates in trilobites. In most insects, the thorax itself is composed of three segments; the prothorax, the mesothorax, and the metathorax.
